- Mysterious Name: a name that doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename.
- Duplicated Code: same logic shape in more than one hunk/file. → extract.
- Feature Envy: a method reaching into another object's data more than its own. → move it.
- Data Clumps: the same few fields/params travelling together. → bundle into a type.
- Primitive Obsession: a primitive standing in for a domain concept. → small type.
- Repeated Switches: the same switch/if-cascade on the same type recurring. → polymorphism or shared map.
- Shotgun Surgery: one logical change forcing scattered edits across many files. → gather.
- Divergent Change: one module edited for several unrelated reasons. → split.
- Speculative Generality: abstraction/params/hooks for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete.

# drops

A cross-project issue tracker for AI coding agents. Go, pure-Go SQLite, and
Cobra; one database for every repository, with the project resolved from the
working directory.

**Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) before working here.** It carries the gate, the
scratch-store rule, the test discipline every ticket is held to, and the tools in
this environment that report success while failing.

Issues live in **GitHub Issues** on
[`tedkulp/drops`](https://github.com/tedkulp/drops), driven by the `gh` CLI —
not in the `drops` store this repo builds. `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is the
contract for working them; the open queue there is the work queue, and
checked-in notes are not a parallel plan.

The `dw32p` rewrite map that carried this repo to 0.2.0 is closed. Its 79 issues
stay in `~/.drops/drops.db`, which is why `dw32p.N` ids appear in `CHANGELOG.md`
and `docs/research/`.

380	Single-context: `CONTEXT.md` at the root, ADRs under `docs/adr/` once there are
381	any. See [docs/agents/domain.md](docs/agents/domain.md).
382	
383	### Which skill for what
384	
385	`codebase-design` for package shape and seams, `tdd` for build tickets, `grilling`
386	plus `domain-modeling` for decision tickets.
387	
388	## The gate
389	
390	`just test-all`: `go vet` and a gofmt check, then `go test ./... -race`. A green
391	`go test` is not a green build.
392	
393	CI runs this **recipe**, not a copy of it. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` installs
394	`just` and calls `just test-all`, because a workflow that wrote the steps out
395	would be a second gate free to drift from this one — and a hand-rolled `go test`
396	step would drop the `DROPS_DB` tripwire below without saying so. `release_test.go`
397	holds the workflow to the recipe. A second CI job runs `goreleaser check`, so a
398	broken `.goreleaser.yaml` is found on a push rather than on a tag.
399	
400	The gofmt check formats what **git** counts as part of this tree — tracked files
401	plus untracked ones git would offer to add — and not everything under `.`. So an
402	unformatted `.go` file left in the gitignored `/.scratch/` does not fail the gate,
403	while a new file you have not run `git add` on still does. "What git counts" means
404	git's whole exclude set, not `.gitignore` alone: `.git/info/exclude` and your
405	`core.excludesFile` are read too, so the gate's view of this tree is exactly `git
406	status`'s view, and the untracked half of that is as machine-specific as `git
407	status` is. Tracked files are not — `--cached` ignores excludes.
408	
409	The vet half has the mirror-image trap, and the gate now covers it. `./...` is
410	not every package in this tree: the go tool drops `testdata` directories from
411	that pattern, and any directory whose name begins with `.` or `_`. So
412	`internal/lockfile/testdata/holder` — the real second process the lockfile
413	contention tests build and run, not sample data — was formatted but never
414	vetted. The gate vets those packages by path, and the set is **derived** as the
415	directories git counts minus the ones `go list ./...` reports, rather than by
416	naming `testdata`, so a helper added under any skipped directory is vetted on
417	arrival. Directories under a nested `go.mod` are excluded, because `go vet`
418	refuses a path in another module and `tools/mutate/testdata/fixture` is a
419	deliberately-mutated corpus for the mutate tool's own tests.
420	
421	`test` and `mutate` export `DROPS_DB` to `/dev/null/no-default-store-in-tests/drops.db`
422	— not a scratch store but a tripwire, so a test that reaches for `store.DefaultPath()`
423	fails with ENOTDIR and names the path. Since the cutover (`dw32p.28`) this is the
424	**only** thing between a test and the real store: the binary this repository builds
425	owns `~/.drops/drops.db`, so `internal/store`'s development guard is gone and nothing
426	in runtime code refuses that path any more. Issues live in the store the suite must
427	never open.
428	
429	Four tools lie about success here:
430	
431	- `gofmt -l` exits zero while listing files. The file list is the signal, never `$?`.
432	- `grep -c` exits one on zero matches and silently skips the rest of an `&&` chain.
433	- `go test` prints `ok` for a package whose tests all skipped. Read the skip count
434	  and the test events before treating that output as proof.
435	- `go run` exits 1 whatever its program exited, printing `exit status 3` to stderr.
436	  A recipe that needs the program's own exit code must `go build` and run the binary.
437	
438	## Test discipline
439	
440	The dominant defect in this codebase is a test that appears to cover a requirement
441	but **cannot fail for it**. Coverage does not detect it: `render` and `resolve` sit
442	at 100% function coverage and mutation still found defects in both. Annotated
443	red-checks found zero holes across the reference build; unannotated mutation found
444	every one.
445	
446	So the standard is not a number. It is that each requirement has a **control** — the
447	production branch that makes it true — and that control has been mutated with the
448	test observed **red**.
449	
450	### Which controls get mutated
451	
452	One per **requirement clause**: a behavioural claim the ticket's question names. Not
453	one per test function — that turns the count into the goal and selects for cheap
454	mutations.
455	
456	Where a clause is too coarse to mutate in one place, split it by **load-bearing
457	branch**: parsers, orderings, comparisons, conflict resolution, guards, refusals.
458	Those are where a wrong implementation still passes. A struct that round-trips does
459	not need a control; a comparator does.
460	
461	### How a mutation is run
462	
463	`just mutate`. The four steps are the recipe's, not yours:
464	
465	1. Snapshot the file and record its checksum.
466	2. Apply the mutation.
467	3. Run the one named test, expecting failure. A pass is the finding: the test does
468	   not cover the clause — fix the test, not the record.
469	4. Restore from the snapshot and verify the checksum matches.
470	
471	The snapshot is harness-owned, so **you no longer have to commit first**. `git
472	checkout` was never the restore here — a restore command cannot distinguish a
473	mutation from uncommitted work — and the harness never runs one. A run killed
474	between steps 2 and 4 leaves a journal naming exactly what to put back; the next
475	run refuses to start, and `just mutate --restore` finishes it.
476	
477	Controls live beside the code they mutate, in each package's `mutations.json`: a
478	name, the requirement clause it proves, the file, the `old` → `new` edit, and the
479	test. `just mutate` runs every one; `just mutate core` scopes to a package or a
480	single control name; `--list` prints what is catalogued without running it; and
481	`--file/--old/--new/--test/--clause` runs one ad hoc, for while you are still
482	finding out whether a test can fail at all.
483	
484	It refuses more than it accepts, and every refusal is a finding, never a pass:
485	
486	| It says | It means |
487	|---|---|
488	| `GREEN` | the test passed with the branch broken, so it does not cover the clause |
489	| `NOT RUN` | no test of that name ran — `go test -run` matching nothing prints `ok` and exits 0 |
490	| `BUILD FAILED` | the mutation does not compile, so it proves nothing about the test |
491	| `NO MATCH` | `old` is absent or appears twice; a mutation must name exactly one branch |
492	| `BASELINE RED` | the test was already failing, so its red says nothing |
493	
494	Exit 0 means every control went red, 1 that there is a finding, 2 that it was
495	called wrong, and **3 that a restore failed and the tree may still hold a
496	mutation**.
497	
498	`just mutate` is deliberately not part of `test-all`. The gate asks whether this
499	commit is green; mutation asks whether the suite can fail, and pays a compile per
500	control to answer. Run it when a ticket adds or changes a control.
501	
502	### What a ticket records
503	
504	Enumerate, in `close --reason`: each control (file and behaviour), the test that went
505	red, and confirmation of the restore. `just mutate <package>` prints exactly that, so
506	the enumeration is a by-product rather than prose written from memory, and `--json` is
507	the same record for a machine. A bare count is unauditable — it is the form that let a
508	ticket record "one control" without anyone reading it as "one".
509	
510	A control that is not in a `mutations.json` was proved once and can never be proved
511	again. Catalogue it.
512	
513	### Seams
514	
515	**Discovered facts become constructor parameters; real subsystems stay real.**
516	
517	A fact a process learns about its environment — the writer, terminal-ness, measured
518	width, the pager, the clock, the ID source — is a struct field passed in, never
519	discovered at the point of use. `render` accepts all four of its environment facts,
520	so its whole suite is byte-exact literals with no fake anywhere; the reference build
521	discovered them and needed two package-level variables to make the same behaviour
522	reachable.
523	
524	The datastore is not such a fact. There is deliberately no `Store` interface: every
525	test runs against real temp SQLite, real git, and real `flock`. `synctest` cannot
526	fake SQLite's busy-handler sleep, so lock-contention tests are real-clock. Making
527	these fakeable would trade a real defect class for a faster suite.
528	
529	### Serialized contracts
530	
531	For at least one case per serialized contract, run the real writer and decode its
532	bytes. Deriving both sides from the same description tests the description.
533	
534	### The CLI is a contract
535	
536	`docs/cli-contract.md` is what agents read to drive drops. A verb that
537	changes shape without that file changing is a defect.
538	
539	Every command in the tree carries at least one boundary test through
540	`RunForTest(args, db, cwd)`, asserting what the doc says a reader observes: a
541	byte-exact row for a scanning verb, the JSON shape for a reading verb, the store
542	effect for a mutating verb. A census test walks the command tree and fails on any
543	command absent from the tested-verb registry, so skipping one is an edit to a visible
544	list rather than an omission.
545	
546	## Changelog
547	
548	`CHANGELOG.md` follows Keep a Changelog. Every change made after the latest
549	release goes under `## [Unreleased]` (create it when absent), grouped under the
550	appropriate change category. Only release work moves those entries into a dated
551	version section.
552	
553	## Lessons retained from the reference build
554	
555	- Re-check the premise before the next round of rigour, not after it.
556	- Measure before changing a documented fact. A confidently wrong count is worse than
557	  a stale one.
558	
559	## Planning
560	
561	This repository has no `.internal/` tree. Durable research belongs in `docs/`; live
562	plans and decisions belong in the issue tracker. The local `.gitignore` deliberately
563	overrides the workstation's global `.internal/` exclusion so accidental files cannot
564	disappear from status.

I found no hard violations of the documented standards. Everything below is a judgement call. I didn't modify anything.

**Documented standards: all met**
- **"The CLI is a contract"** (`AGENTS.md`): `docs/cli-contract.md` gains the scroll, range and empty-hint text in the same diff as the code.
- **"Changelog"** (`AGENTS.md`): the entry sits under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added`. The entry just above it ends with "See the contract's [The board]"; this one has no link. That's a style gap, not a rule breach.
- **"Which controls get mutated"** (`AGENTS.md`): there are 7 new controls, split by branch (scroll-to-cursor vs. one card at a time, `>` vs `>=`, 1-based, both directions of `col == colClosed`, the `len(cards) == 0` guard). This follows the #14 marker precedent, and the `note` is extended.
  - Soft gap: the contract says the hint is "dimmed", and `TestAnEmptyColumnKeepsItsHeadingAndShowsAHint` checks that, but no catalogued control covers `dimStyle.Render(...emptyHint...)`. The "catalogue it" rule arguably wants one.
  - Worth knowing: `cardTop` and the scrolling already existed at HEAD. This diff adds its first direct controls and documents it, so the changelog's "Added" wording slightly overstates what's new.
- **Test idiom:** the "The clause:" comments, the `testcase` table variable and the "this mode proves nothing" guards all match the surrounding tests.

**Smells (all judgement calls)**
- **`internal/tui/board.go`**
  - **Data Clumps:** `heading(col column, count, top, fit int, focused bool)`. `top` and `fit` are always worked out as a pair (`fit := cardsFit(height); top := cardTop(...)`), here and in `switchColumn`. A small window type would carry both.
  - **Repeated Switches:** `emptyHint` branches on `col == colClosed`, next to the `columnNames` array indexed by column. A `[columnCount]string` array for the hints would match that idiom.
- **`internal/tui/board_test.go`**
  - **Mysterious Name:** in `for index, title := range pane.cards[colReady]`, `title` holds a whole row, which gives `title.title`. `card` or `candidate` would fit what `board.go` uses.
  - **Mysterious Name:** `full := row{...}` means "a column with a card"; `occupied` or `one` would read better.
  - **Duplicated Code:** this block is copied from `TestTabCountsTheRowPositionOnScreen`:
    ```go
    // 12 lines is 9 pane rows: a heading and two cards.
    pane := onBoard(t, fixture, 200, 12)
    ... if fit != 2 { t.Fatalf("a column fits %d cards, want 2 for this test to scroll", fit) }
    ```
    It could become a shared helper.
  - Minor ordering issue: `selected := pane.cards[colReady][pane.cursor.position].title` runs before the check on `pane.cursor.position`. If the cursor were ever out of range, the test would panic instead of failing with its message.
- **`internal/tui/frame_test.go`**
  - **Duplicated Code:** the new "board scrolled down Closed" mode repeats the preceding mode's `press(t, pane, "B")` and shift+tab lines word for word.
  - The id loop and the closed-issue loop in `corpus` both hardcode `12`, and nothing ties them together.
- **`internal/tui/mutations.json`**: nothing to flag. Controls sharing an identical `old` string follow the existing precedent (`tab-lands-on-the-nearest-row` and `tab-counts-the-row-on-screen`).
